To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most important trends in clinical chemistry automation are represented by the development of the microfluidics technology, by the introduction of the micro total analysis systems (μTAS) and by the development of high throughput screening (HTS) methods for the identification and characterization of new biomarkers.
(1) the use of automation in clinical chemistry is increasing and (2) automation has a positive influence on laboratory efficiency and on patient care.

the main technological and organisational features of clinical chemistry automation have been presented and discussed; the most relevant advances on the analytical methodology and instrument development have been illustrated; the present state and the future trends of the clinical chemistry automation have also been evaluated.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new analytical methods, based on the use of the most advanced techniques, for the measurement of the most important clinical parameters, and with the design and construction of new automated systems.
the design, construction and testing of a prototype of a fully automated clinical chemistry analyser, which is capable of processing a wide range of routine clinical tests in a continuous flow mode.

the development of a new generation of analytical systems based on the integration of different technologies, including microfabrication, optical detection, and computerized control, in a single instrument.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the automation of clinical chemistry is still in a state of rapid evolution.
automation in clinical chemistry is an irreversible process and that, in the near future, all the clinical chemistry laboratories in the developed countries will be totally automated.

the future will see the development of more sophisticated, more versatile, faster, and more flexible analytical systems, able to perform a large variety of analyses, including those of complex biological samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the automation in clinical laboratory has been a great success and it will continue to be so.
the automation in clinical laboratories has been achieved and that the main problems to be solved are now related to the quality of analytical results.
the automation of clinical chemistry procedures has reached a high level of maturity and is now a consolidated and widely used technology in clinical laboratories.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the future will be dominated by the use of microfluidic devices and by the development of new analytical methods and instruments based on them.
the future of clinical chemistry is automation, and the future of automation is in clinical chemistry.

, in the future, automation will become more and more important in the field of clinical chemistry, and that it will be necessary to have a more integrated approach to automation, in order to obtain the best results.
